body:
Full-codebase review, wire-contract gaps. Every item verified against the implementation.

Missing rules — a client author cannot implement correctly from the contract alone:
* The same-name merge is not documented at all. On a shopping or checklist list, two live items whose names match case-insensitively are merged into one survivor (earliest created_at, then smaller id), per-field LWW across the group, losers tombstoned with a server-authored clock. The only mention anywhere is the aside that it never runs on a ledger. A client can get back a tombstone it never wrote and another row's fields changed, with no documented reason.
* Clock clamping: a field's `updated_at` and a row's `created_at` are silently capped at server-now + 1 hour, so a device with a fast clock has writes re-stamped and a write it believes won comes back losing.
* `updated_by` is documented as "a device UUID", but the server writes the reserved literal `server-merge` on merge tombstones.
* `POST /sync` can answer `403 not_a_member` when `full_lists` names a list the caller is not on; the Sync section lists only 410, `too_many_changes`, `invalid_full_lists` and `unknown_list`. Neither client can quarantine it (see the separate ticket about that refusal also rolling back the push).
* The per-field input caps on `/sync` are only partly documented (id 128, updated_by 128, name 500, category 200, quantity 200, item note 5000, price amount 32 chars, currency 16, stores/category_order 200 entries of 200 chars). Neither client enforces any of them, so a pasted 600-character name is accepted by both UIs and then refused.

Stale or wrong statements:
* The app-package section says the Android client polls `/app-version` when its settings screen opens; it has been the About screen since T-224.
* It says a client refused with 426 reads `/app-version`'s `protocol` to learn what to catch up to. No client parses it — Android's DTO omits the field and the web never reads it from the envelope either.
* `GET /lists` is documented but dead: the web has an unused wrapper, Android has no method for it.
* `device_label` and `created_at` are both optional in practice but presented as required.
title: Wire contract: the same-name merge, clock clamping and the sync input caps are undocumented
